llm.reply:
The gene NCBIGene:4292, name: mutL homolog 1 [1]. It is associated with the disease Colorectal cancer, hereditary nonpolyposis, type 2 [3]. Meanwhile, the gene NCBIGene:4436, name: mutS homolog 2 is linked to Lynch syndrome 1 [5][6].

## Associated Syndromes
The gene NCBIGene:4292 is linked to Muir-TorrÃ© syndrome [1][2]. It is also implicated in Mismatch repair cancer syndrome 1 [4]. In comparison, NCBIGene:4436 is connected to Mismatch repair cancer syndrome 2 [5][7].

## Biological Function
The gene symbol is MLH1 [8]. This gene was found to be recurrently altered in hereditary nonpolyposis colon cancer [18: "identified as a locus frequently mutated in hereditary nonpolyposis colon cancer (HNPCC)"]. Its product partners with another factor to form a complex active in the repair machinery [18: "heterodimerize with mismatch repair endonuclease PMS2 to form MutL alpha, part of the DNA mismatch repair system"].

## Clinical Evidence
The variant NM_000249.4(MLH1):c.1418A>T (p.His473Leu) is cataloged for this repair gene [23]. Relevant clinical investigations include the Study of MK-3475 in Patients With Microsatellite Unstable (MSI) Tumors (Cohorts A, B and C) [19]. In addition, screening strategies are addressed by Stand up to Cancer: MAGENTA (Making Genetic Testing Accessible) [29].

Gene NCBIGene:4292, named mutL homolog 1, and gene NCBIGene:4436, named mutS homolog 2, are mismatch repair genes associated with hereditary cancer predisposition [1][5]. Disruption of mutL homolog 1 is linked to Muir-TorrÃ© syndrome, Colorectal cancer, hereditary nonpolyposis, type 2, and Mismatch repair cancer syndrome 1 [2][3][4]. In comparison, mutS homolog 2 is linked to Lynch syndrome 1 and Mismatch repair cancer syndrome 2 [6][7].

## Molecular Function

The gene symbol is MLH1 [8]. The gene name is MLH1 [12]. The OMIM entry title is DNA MISMATCH REPAIR PROTEIN MLH1; MLH1 [11]. The MLH1 product partners with PMS2 to create MutL alpha for mismatch repair [18: "heterodimerize with mismatch repair endonuclease PMS2 to form MutL alpha, part of the DNA mismatch repair system"]. MutL alpha introduces strand incisions when bound alongside MutS complexes [18: "When MutL alpha is bound by MutS beta and some accessory proteins, the PMS2 subunit of MutL alpha introduces a single-strand break near DNA mismatches"]. MLH1 also associates with MLH3 to yield MutL gamma for meiotic processes [18: "heterodimerize with DNA mismatch repair protein MLH3 to form MutL gamma, which is involved in meiosis"]. The gene is recurrently altered in inherited colorectal malignancies [18: "frequently mutated in hereditary nonpolyposis colon cancer (HNPCC)"]. It is annotated under meiotic mismatch repair, mismatch repair, and response to stress [15][21][26].

## Clinical Variants

Investigated variants include NM_000249.4(MLH1):c.545+1271_677+737delinsCA [10]. Another ClinVar entry is NM_000249.4(MLH1):c.453+625_545+920delinsT [17]. Further described alleles include NM_000249.4(MLH1):c.1418A>T (p.His473Leu) and NM_000249.4(MLH1):c.884+5T>A [23][28].

## Published Evidence

Functional assays in yeast and in vitro systems evaluate MLH1 variants [9]. Methylation tolerance assays characterize variants of uncertain significance in MLH1 and MSH2 in Lynch syndrome [22]. Lynch syndrome tumors may display concurrent MLH1 germline mutations and somatic promoter hypermethylation [16]. Screened endometrial carcinomas also demonstrate MLH1/PMS2 deficiency alongside MLH1 hypermethylation [27]. Relevant literature is indexed under PMID 17510385, PMID 17973250, PMID 30998989, and PMID 33577226 [14][20][25][30].

## Associated Studies

The IMPACT Study - Identification of Men With a Genetic Predisposition to ProstAte Cancer evaluates targeted cancer predisposition [13]. Therapeutic trials include Study of MK-3475 in Patients With Microsatellite Unstable (MSI) Tumors (Cohorts A, B and C) [19]. Prevention strategies are addressed in Surgery in Preventing Ovarian Cancer in Patients With Genetic Mutations [24]. Diagnostic implementation is explored in Stand up to Cancer: MAGENTA (Making Genetic Testing Accessible) [29].
